result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cmty_fast_greedy()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Detect communities using Fast Greedy (Clauset-Newman-Moore) algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L10692-L10807){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cmty_fast_greedy( attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is a greedy modularity optimization algorithm that merges communities to maximize modularity. It's efficient for medium to large graphs and provides good quality communities. Only works with undirected graphs. Algorithm: 1. start with each node in its own community 2. build a heap of merge candidates ordered by modularity gain (ΔQ) 3. repeatedly merge the pair with highest ΔQ until no improvement 4. return the partition with maximum modularity ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : column name to store community assignments in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `cmty_fast_greedy`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to community IDs (0-indexed). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is directed (requires undirected graph). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Fast Greedy (Clauset, Newman, and Moore, 2004) maintains a heap of merge candidates ranked by the modularity gain $\Delta Q$ their union would produce, repeatedly pops the top pair, and stops once every candidate merge would strictly decrease modularity. The resulting partition is the one of maximum modularity along that greedy trajectory. On sparse graphs the heap bookkeeping runs in $O(n \log^2 n)$ time with $O(n + m)$ memory, which made it the first modularity optimizer usable on graphs of a few hundred thousand nodes. Modern alternatives like Louvain (`cmty_louvain()`) typically reach higher modularity at similar or better cost, but Fast Greedy remains attractive when a strictly agglomerative dendrogram is useful. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two disconnected triangles are the clearest possible case: each becomes its own community, with no edges at all between them: ::: {#efbe7c42 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") # Clique 1 .add_edge("D", "E") # Clique 2 ) communities = graph.cmty_fast_greedy(return_dict=True) len(set(communities.values())) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Storing the result as a node attribute and chaining into `colorize_node_attrs()` visualizes the communities directly: ::: {#8d571716 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="A") # Clique 1 .add_edge(source="D", target="E") # Clique 2 ) ( graph .cmty_fast_greedy(attr_name="community") .colorize_node_attrs(node_attr_from="community", palette="Set1") .describe() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 5 Number of edges : 4 Directed : False Density : 0.40 Average degree (min, max) : 1.60 (1, 2) Connected : False Number of connected components : 2 Tree : False Bipartite : False Computations on nodes: - cmty_fast_greedy() -> attr: 'community' (5 of 5 nodes) Node aesthetics: - color <- community via colorize (palette: "Set1") (values: #377eb8, #e41a1c, 5 of 5 nodes) ``` ::: :::
